clue.text: Bowled too short a wood

parts.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: too means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A cricket complaint: the bowler pitched it too short, off a piece of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the last letter from the synonym of 'too'. The surface reads as a cricket ball pitched short, but 'a' just supplies its own letter before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light timber from a tropical American tree, used for models.

clue.text: Temple's block has inner compound

indicators.note: has inner says the block word holds the compound inside it

parts.note: to block something is to ban it
silica is the chemical compound silicon dioxide

explanation.surface: A building's stone block contains some chemical compound.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to a basilica, a type of church or temple, so it matches a possessive.

clue.text: Unstuffy, with latest in apparel?

indicators.note: latest in picks out the final letter of the word apparel

parts.note: a room that is not stuffy is airy

explanation.surface: Someone relaxed and fresh, dressed in the newest fashions.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: AIRY (unstuffy) with L, the last letter of 'apparel', describes someone flashily dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for flashy or showily dressed, someone relaxed who sports the latest gear.

clue.text: A nit drinking what is needed for pub

indicators.note: drinking means the insect word takes the other in, swallowing it

parts.note: a nit is the egg of a louse, loosely the insect itself
Eh? is an exclamation meaning What?

explanation.surface: A head louse needs a drink, so off to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is needed for' is only link padding. A nit is strictly a louse's egg, but crosswords freely use it for the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An alehouse is an old word for a pub or tavern.

clue.text: Readjust after moving European native to Med

indicators.note: after moving says the letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to rearrange a European plant until it suits the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: READJUST plus E are rearranged by 'after moving' to give the two-word plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Judas tree, Cercis siliquastrum, is a flowering tree that grows wild around the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Female article removed from prison line

indicators.note: removed from says the article is taken out of the prison word

parts.note: jail means prison
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A woman's article has been confiscated from a prison queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed from' takes A out of JAIL, leaving JIL, and L is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A jill is a female ferret, and the word also means a girl or woman.

clue.text: Spooner's pot dispensing tea

indicators.note: Spooner's signals that the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: a jar is a pot or container
dealing out cards is dispensing them

explanation.surface: Someone's teapot is pouring out tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of JAR and DEALING to get 'dar-jealing', which is said like the tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Darjeeling is a fine black tea from the Indian hill district of that name.

clue.text: In spot, bit upset, but calm

indicators.note: In says the turned word goes inside the spot word

parts.note: to spot something is to see it

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: Even when a pimple is a bit inflamed, stay calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spot' reads as a pimple, but it is the verb meaning notice; in a down clue 'upset' turns the little bit upside down before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means composed and unhurried, a synonym of calm.

clue.text: Teddy girl left without stuffing under jumpers

indicators.note: under in a down clue places the girl and the rest below the jumpers

parts.note: roos, short for kangaroos, are jumpers
Eve is a girl's name

indicators.note: without stuffing removes the inside of the word left, keeping its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A girl's teddy bear has lost its stuffing and lies under some sweaters.
explanation.walkthrough: The teddy bear was named after US President Theodore 'Teddy' Roosevelt, so 'Teddy' is a name, not a toy; in a down clue 'under' places the girl and the trimmed word beneath the jumpers.
explanation.definitionFit: Teddy was the nickname of Theodore Roosevelt, 26th President of the United States.

clue.text: Material for key point not fleshed out

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass
something with no flesh on it is bony

explanation.surface: The key point of an argument is left undeveloped.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'key' is a piano key: the black keys were traditionally made of this dark wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is the dense black wood traditionally used for the black keys of a piano.

clue.text: Dickens character to see Pickwick's man around four, not in the morning

indicators.note: not in the morning removes the abbreviation for morning, as in 9 am
around means the servant's name goes round the numeral

parts.note: Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's servant in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An instruction to visit Mr Pickwick's valet some time after four in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: The morning abbreviation sits inside the servant's full name, so dropping it joins his initial to his surname. 'to see' is link padding; Dick Swiveller is in The Old Curiosity Shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick Swiveller is the good-natured clerk in Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop.

clue.text: Couple married at old Roman church

parts.note: a duo is a couple, a pair

explanation.surface: A newly married pair at an ancient church in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Duomo is the Italian name for a cathedral church, so an apt label for an Italian church.

clue.text: Kept down, not cloth, for half of pillow

parts.note: the cloth means the clergy, so people not of the cloth are the lay

indicators.note: half of takes the second three letters of the word pillow

explanation.surface: Someone lies low without bedding, using only half a pillow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cloth' is the clergy, so 'not cloth' is LAY; the back half of PILLOW is LOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie low is to keep out of sight; lay low is its past tense, meaning kept down.

clue.text: Hide — retreating, say, when going gets tough

annotationWithheld.why: Hide — retreating, say, when going gets tough: LEATHER (hide) is clear but no parse of 'retreating, say' gives the final Y, and the clue cannot be traced online
annotationWithheld.clue: Hide — retreating, say, when going gets tough

clue.text: A top is then adjusted to this

definitions.text: A top is then adjusted to this

indicators.note: adjusted says the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hat is put on and then straightened.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange A TOP IS THEN; the whole clue is also the definition, since lifting a hat is how one acknowledges someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipping a hat means lifting or touching its top in greeting, an adjustment of the top hat.

clue.text: Good to put away mobiles etc going off

indicators.note: going off says the letters explode into a new order, as a bomb goes off

explanation.surface: It's sensible to put away phones and other gadgets that start ringing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good to put away' reads as advice about phones, but it means food fit to eat; MOBILES ETC are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Comestible means edible, fit to eat, so something good to swallow down.

clue.text: Turner working at Flatford

parts.note: reads as the painter J M W Turner at work in Constable country, but means a thing that turns at Flatford Mill

explanation.surface: The painter Turner is busy at Flatford, a spot made famous by his rival Constable.
explanation.walkthrough: Flatford Mill in Suffolk is the subject of Constable's paintings; the 'turner' there is the wheel that drives the mill.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill's wheel turns in the stream to power it, so it is the turner at work at a mill.

clue.text: Race punt round lake

indicators.note: round says the wager word goes around the lake letter

parts.note: punt means a bet or wager
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A race in which punts go round a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' suggests a flat boat, but here it is a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: To belt is informal for racing along at great speed.

clue.text: Two camps so divided by call for cutting off head

indicators.note: divided by says the so word is split with the other word inside it

parts.note: so means thus, therefore

indicators.note: cutting off head removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: to call for something is to demand it

explanation.surface: Two rival camps are split over a demand for an execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting off head' leaves EMAND, which divides THUS to make TH(EMAND)US.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a society split into two opposing camps, insiders and outsiders.

clue.text: Music from Judge Dread touring Cockney has heard

indicators.note: touring says the judge and dread letters go round the sounded word

parts.note: funk is an old word for fear or dread

indicators.note: heard means the dropped-H word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a Cockney drops the H of has, saying 'as

explanation.surface: A soundtrack from the comic hero Judge Dredd's visit to a Cockney.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys drop their Hs, so 'has' is said 'as, which sounds like the letters entered. The surface evokes the comic hero Judge Dredd, though 'Dread' here means fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Jazz-funk is a style of music blending jazz improvisation with funk rhythms.

clue.text: Orphan girl starts off visiting underworld

indicators.note: starts off removes the first letter of each of the two words

parts.note: someone visiting the underworld is in hell

explanation.surface: An orphaned girl begins a trip to the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts off' drops the first letters of IN and HELL, leaving N and ELL. Little Nell is the orphan heroine of The Old Curiosity Shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Nell, the orphaned heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop, is a girl called by this name.

clue.text: To start campaigning Ben first put sign up

annotationWithheld.why: To start campaigning Ben first put sign up: JOIN (sign up) is clear but no reading of 'Ben first put' gives BATTLE; the OCR text appears garbled and cannot be traced online
annotationWithheld.clue: To start campaigning Ben first put sign up

clue.text: Tramp — one no longer wrapped in papers

indicators.note: no longer wrapped in says the one is no longer inside the papers word

parts.note: a dossier is a file of papers
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A homeless man, once a bundle of newspapers kept him warm, no longer.
explanation.walkthrough: Tramps were said to sleep wrapped in newspapers; taking I out of DOSSIER gives the slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosser is British slang for a homeless person who sleeps rough.

clue.text: Snow base for tour operator

indicators.note: tour says the letters travel round into a new order

explanation.surface: Snow at the bottom of the slopes for a ski holiday company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tour operator' reads as one phrase but splits: 'tour' shuffles SNOW BASE and 'operator' is a surgeon; 'for' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawbones is a jocular slang term for a surgeon, someone who operates.

clue.text: Cut grass

definitions.meaning: to cut something is to divide it into parts
to grass is British slang for informing on someone to the police

explanation.definitionFit: Split means divided by cutting, and in slang it means to inform on an accomplice.

clue.text: A boy in enthusiasm cut shrub

indicators.note: in says the boy goes inside the shortened word
cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: zeal means enthusiasm
Al is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad whose enthusiasm for gardening led him to prune a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthusiasm cut' looks like a phrase about losing interest, but it is the synonym of enthusiasm with its last letter dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: An azalea is a flowering shrub of the rhododendron family.

clue.text: Made strides — took van round work

indicators.note: round says the led word goes around the work

parts.note: to take the van is to lead, so took van means led
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone drove a van on a round of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' here is the vanguard, the front: to take the van is to lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Loped means ran with long bounding strides.

clue.text: Tart with cape wearing a badge

indicators.note: wearing says the cape sits within the A and the badge

parts.note: an ID is an identity badge
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A tart in a cape with a badge pinned on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' is the sour taste, not a pastry or a woman; C goes inside A ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Tart means sour or sharp in taste, as acid is.

clue.text: City side not exposed by forwards in last quarter

parts.note: the lee side is the side sheltered from the wind

indicators.note: in last quarter takes the final two of the eight letters of forwards

explanation.surface: A football club's defence is protected by its forwards late in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forwards' sounds like football players, but its last quarter supplies DS; 'by' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a major city in West Yorkshire, in the north of England.

clue.text: Yokel cut and bled and had fit after quick drink?

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a hick is a country yokel
cupping was an old treatment that bled patients, so cupped means bled

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin is wounded, bleeding, and has a fit after a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Cupping was the old medical practice of drawing blood with heated cups.
explanation.definitionFit: Gulping a drink too fast can bring on a fit of spasms of the diaphragm, which is what this word describes.

clue.text: Bore in English class ordered outside

indicators.note: outside says the ordered word goes around the others

parts.note: to be told is to be ordered
a rate is a class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A dull pupil in an English lesson is sent out of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a dull person, but it is the past tense of bear: endured.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore, past tense of bear, means put up with, endured.

clue.text: Credit card finally accepted in backward marketplace

indicators.note: accepted in says the letter is taken inside the reversed word
backward means the market word is read in reverse

parts.note: a souk is an Arab marketplace

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of card

explanation.surface: A bazaar where a credit card is at last accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: A souk is a market in Arab countries. 'Credit' reads as the card's credit, but it is the definition: praise earned.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudos means credit or prestige earned for an achievement.
